note: Occupancy start per seat. Each carries the document that states it.

cohort_2022.document: Journal of the County Council, Tuesday January 10 2023 -- https://stlouisco.civicweb.net/document/110433?printPdf=true (meeting Id 800)
cohort_2022.quote: County Executive Page: "Today, in Memorial Plaza, we had a moment to celebrate ... the word inauguration means an official beginning." Councilwoman Days: "the inauguration. It was a very nice event this morning."
cohort_2022.caveat: Charter 2.040/3.010/5.040/6.050 compute the first Tuesday of January = 2023-01-03. The inauguration was 2023-01-10 and the roll call that night seats all seven. 2023-01-10 is the first date a DOCUMENT places them in the seat; it is not asserted to be the legal term start.

cohort_2024.document: Journal of the County Council, Tuesday January 7 2025 -- https://stlouisco.civicweb.net/document/388825?printPdf=true (meeting Id 25750)
cohort_2024.quote: Councilman Harder: "We had a great swearing-in ceremony this morning." Councilman Archer: "It was a very special day for getting inaugurated." Roll call names all seven, Archer included.
cohort_2024.caveat: 2025-01-07 was also the charter first Tuesday, so the document and the computed day agree here.

prosecuting_attorney.quote: "Melissa Price Smith was sworn in on Friday, January 3, 2025, as the St. Louis County Prosecuting Attorney."
prosecuting_attorney.caveat: Wesley Bell won the seat in Nov 2022 and then won a US House seat. Charter 5.050 fills the vacancy by county executive appointment with council confirmation. Price Smith is NOT the certified winner.

open: Sam Page has been County Executive since 2019 and Jake Zimmerman Assessor since 2011. Countywide seats carry no map floor, so their occupancy could reach further back than 2023-01-10 -- but no document for the earlier dates has been read yet.
